_meta.indication: Prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2/3 randomized (2:1), double-blinded, placebo-controlled, two cohort design trial
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy preterm and term infants from birth up to 1 year entering their first RSV season
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Incidence of RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection (MALRI) from Days 1 through 150 postdose
pivotal_trials.result: Observed efficacy for RSV-associated MALRI was 60.4% (95% CI: 44.1%, 71.9%; p<0.001); key secondary endpoint of RSV-associated hospitalization showed a relative risk reduction of 84.2% (95% CI: 66.6%, 92.6%, p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), active-controlled (palivizumab) study conducted in two parts: Part 1 is double-blind and Part 2 is open-label; primary endpoint was safety, with efficacy and PK as secondary endpoints
pivotal_trials.population: Infants at increased risk for severe RSV disease (e.g., chronic lung disease, congenital heart disease, prematurity) from birth up to 1 year entering their first RSV season
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was safety; RSV-associated MALRI (Days 1 through 150) was a secondary endpoint
pivotal_trials.result: Incidence rates of RSV-associated MALRI were comparable between clesrovimab (3.6%, 95% CI: 2.0%, 6.0%) and palivizumab (3.0%, 95% CI: 1.6%, 5.3%); the trial was not powered to detect differences

key_safety: Generally well tolerated; most common adverse reactions were injection-site erythema (3.7%), injection-site swelling (2.7%) and rash (2.3%); key concerns are potential serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) and serious skin reactions
target_moa: A monoclonal antibody that preferentially binds the prefusion conformation of the RSV fusion (F) protein at antigenic Site IV, locking the protein in its prefusion state and preventing membrane fusion and viral entry

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because the drug is not first in class and did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues

requirement.text: 4841-2 Conduct a surveillance study of current and emerging respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) variants from global locations, with F protein sequencing and identification of clesrovimab binding site substitutions and their frequency.

citations.quote: 4841-2 Conduct a surveillance study of current and emerging respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) variants from global locations, with F protein sequencing and identification of clesrovimab binding site substitutions and their frequency. These surveillance activities should include active collection and characterization of RSV samples from global regions (i.e., North America [US/Canada], Europe, rest of the world) and will target at least 100 samples from each region when fully operational, as well as periodic analysis of sequences from public databases (i.e., GISAID, NCBI, GenBank). The surveillance study should also determine the cell culture neutralization activity of clesrovimab against those RSV clesrovimab binding epitope variants carrying substitutions (VAF >10%) and with unknown impact on clesrovimab susceptibility that are capable of growing in cell culture. Phenotypic characterization will include RSV variants whose prevalence is \ge 5\% within an RSV season (or over two consecutive years in public databases) and/or \ge 3-fold increase above 1% from the previous season across all sequenced samples and from all sites within a global region. RSV variants of interest for phenotypic testing will include those carrying substitutions of unknown impact on clesrovimab susceptibility, detected in Site IV, adjacent to the clesrovimab binding epitope (within \le 5 Å distance), or outside Site IV at highly conserved positions (\ge 99\% in GenBank).
